newsitem.title: USA: Physician Support stock plunges after warning.
newsitem.headline: Physician Support stock plunges after warning.

text.p: Shares of Physician Support Systems Inc. lost more than half their value Friday, a day after the provider of business management services to doctors and hospitals warned of disappointing fourth-quarter earnings.
The stock tumbled $9.06 to $7.50 on Nasdaq, where it was the day's biggest loser.

Physician Support said late Thursday it expected to break even in the fourth-quarter before merger and restructuring costs. Analysts on average had expected the company to earn 15 cents a share, according to a First Call survey.
The company reported a loss of $2.3 million, or 5 cents a share, on revenues of $17.9 million in the quarter ended Sept. 30.
Physician Support sees fourth-quarter revenues of about $21 million and $74 million for the year ended Dec. 31.
The company, based in Mt. Joy, Pa., said unexpected seasonal factors also weakened fourth-quarter earnings.
Still, some analysts said Physician Support's long-term outlook was strong.
"At this price, the company is a terrific buy," said David Francis, an analyst at Punk, Ziegel & Knoell.

Physician Support has been hampered by a lengthy restructuring at its Spring Anaesthesia Group unit. But Francis expects the company to show improvement in the second half of 1997, once the Spring turnaround is completed.
The management of PhyServ is being put in charge of Spring and will help the troubled unit move toward profitability, the company said Thursday.

Francis said the health care information sector market has been hard hit lately due to profit warnings. Over the long-term, however, market fundamentals should pull these stocks out of the doldrums, he said.
Francis lowered his earnings estimate for Physician Support for both 1997 and 1998, but continued to recommend the stock as an "aggressive buy."
Cowen & Co. downgraded the stock to a buy from a strong buy after lowering its earnings estimates for 1997 and 1998, citing uncertainty surrounding the company's Spring restructuring.
